result:
Done. Here's what was wrong and what I fixed in the repo (`app/`, `lib/`):

**The core issue:** this SaaS pivoted from "InboxZap" (email cleanup) to "Lumina" (AI meeting assistant), but the migration was left half-finished, which is why organic traffic is stuck — Google doesn't know what the site is about anymore.

- **Title tag told Google the wrong product.** `app/layout.tsx` still shipped the title/description "InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes" on a homepage whose body copy is entirely about Lumina's meeting assistant. That's the single biggest fix here — a mismatched `<title>` actively suppresses CTR and relevance for every query the homepage could rank for. Fixed to match the real product, and added matching Twitter Card tags and Organization/SoftwareApplication JSON-LD (previously absent from the repo's layout).
- **`/features` and `/pricing` didn't exist in the repo at all** — they were only linked from nav/sitemap. Created both with page-specific metadata (and fixed a duplicate-`<h1>` on Features in the process).
- **The blog was structurally broken.** The index page was a client component that fetched `/api/posts` — a route that doesn't exist, so it always showed "Could not load posts" to users and crawlers got zero server-rendered content. The 12 existing posts had no routes in the repo either, so they were invisible to Next's build/sitemap despite being indexed. Rebuilt the blog as a proper server-rendered app: `lib/posts.ts` holds the content, `app/blog/page.tsx` lists it server-side, `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` statically generates each post with unique title/description/canonical/OG tags (previously missing meta descriptions entirely).
- **`/faq` 404'd everywhere** — every page's nav/footer links to it, and `next.config.js` already redirected it to `/#faq`, but that anchor never existed on the homepage. Added a real FAQ section with `id="faq"` and FAQPage JSON-LD (a shot at rich-snippet CTR).
- **og:image 404'd site-wide**, killing social-share previews. Added a working placeholder at `/img/og-lumina.png`.
- **Sitemap silently omitted all blog posts** (there was a literal `// TODO: include blog posts once...`). Now generated from the same post data, so it stays in sync.

**Strategic call I made rather than forcing silently:** the 12 legacy posts (email cleanup) are 100% off-topic for a meeting-assistant product — that mismatch is *why* they rank page 4–5 despite real search volume, and why their 6 total clicks never convert. Rather than deleting/redirecting that already-indexed content (hard to reverse, and it does carry some brand-relevant impressions), I kept the URLs live, fixed their crawlability, and added a one-line bridge note on each linking back to Lumina, plus an "Is Lumina the same as InboxZap?" FAQ to capture brand-confused searchers. I also seeded two genuinely on-topic posts (meeting notes template, async standups) targeting real Lumina-relevant intent. If you'd rather 301 the legacy posts away entirely to consolidate topical authority faster, that's a bigger one-way call worth discussing before I'd make it.

Verified: `npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit` both pass clean, and I confirmed the rendered output of `/`, `/features`, `/pricing`, `/blog`, `/faq`, and the blog post routes against a local production server.

One unrelated note: `package.json` pins `next@14.2.5`, which npm flags as having a known security vulnerability (patched in a later 14.x). Didn't touch it since it's outside the SEO scope, but worth a bump when convenient.
